title: Consolidate adjustment traces to prevent export collapse on overlapping credits
creator: Miguel Ortega
description: Intermittent disappearance or coalescing of negative invoice lines when coupon/promotional offsets overlap reserved-capacity discounts and transient rate-limit credits. The current export dedupe and line-fingerprinting logic collapses distinct adjustment events into a single export line, causing Stripe/NetSuite to drop or misattribute credits and producing invoice mismatches and incorrect revenue recognition.
updates: 2026-03-05: Triage - on-call billing alerted after customer reported missing negative line items for March invoices. Reproduction steps captured and sample invoices attached to the ticket.

2026-03-06: Root cause hypothesis - export fingerprint uses (customer_id, invoice_day_bucket, amount_abs) which is insufficient when multiple adjustment types overlap in the same bucket. Also observed retry storms generating duplicated adjustment events that are deduped incorrectly by the exporter.

2026-03-07: Spike completed - added 'adjustment_origin' and 'adjustment_sequence' to local export payload and verified Stripe accepts distinct lines with same amount when a unique origin+seq is attached.

2026-03-09: Design decision - update canonical key for invoice-line export to (invoice_id, adjustment_origin, adjustment_sequence, utc_anchor) and surface adjustment_sequence at creation time. Backfill plan drafted for past 90 days using reconciliation worker.

2026-03-10: PR opened - github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/742 (exporter and schema changes). Unit + integration tests added for deterministic ordering and idempotency. Need infra sign-off for migration window.

2026-03-11: Running canary on 'stripe-test' workspace and comparing NetSuite API payloads; observed resolved duplication in canary samples. Preparing rollout plan for 2026-03-18 with a 48-hour monitoring window.
qa_steps: Stage: deploy exporter with new canonical key and enable canary flag for 5% of customers
Generate synthetic scenarios: overlapping coupon+reserved-capacity adjustments within same utc_bucket; simulate retry storm for rate-limit credits
Assert exported payload contains distinct adjustment_origin and adjustment_sequence fields and that NetSuite/Stripe ingest preserves separate lines
Run reconciliation worker on a sample of 100 invoices to verify idempotent re-emission of missing lines
Post-rollout: run revenue parity check between pre-change and post-change exports for 30 days
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy DB migration adding adjustment_sequence (nullable) and exporter change under feature flag
2) Run migration in read-only mode to populate sequences for new adjustments only
3) Enable canary for 5% with tight alerting on billing-export-anomalies dashboard
4) After 48h, ramp to 25% then 100% over 72h if metrics stable
5) Run backfill reconciliation for last 90 days during off-peak window; emit corrective Journal Entries into NetSuite for reconciled invoices
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Migration may cause exporter to emit additional lines leading to momentary duplication in downstream systems. Mitigation: exporter will tag correction lines with 'correction=true' and downstream mapping will map corrections to adjustment-ledgers instead of creating new invoices.
Risk: Long-running backfill could overload NetSuite API. Mitigation: rate-limit backfill and prioritize high-revenue customers first.
Risk: Edge cases with historical refunds. Mitigation: reconciliation worker will include refund detection and skip invoices with finalized_closure flag.
notes_for_support: Customer-facing: If customers query missing credits, provide the billing-reconciliation playbook link and inform them scheduled backfill will reconcile historic invoices; expected resolution window 7-14 days for older invoices.
Internal: Operations runbook added to Slack #oncall-billing with commands to toggle canary_flag and to re-run small backfills.
